chapter: Arranging for Fletcher, Goodman and Barnet
title: Fletcher's wife as copyist, and why Horace never scored in concert pitch
summary: Fletcher's wife copied most of his and Horace's charts. Fletcher scored in concert pitch, hard on copyists, while Horace always wrote transposed parts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You never saw the score again, and, of course, the good part about that you didn't have to extract your score. They had the copies, naturally, and of course, Fletcher's wife was quite instrumental in that; she was an excellent
And she did most of Fletcher's, and she copied mine. Fletcher scored in concert, which is rough on a copyist.
Right, cause they had to transpose.
Transpose. But I never did. I've never scored in concert yet.

I've always scored in front of the instrument as you copy what you see, because I had -- I'll tell you what started me doing that too, I later got some copyists, and they begin to ask me is it a concert or so and so, and if it was a concert, they'd turn you down. A lot of them didn't know how to transpose, actually, but they had things set up for that.
